name: Two-Pass Depth Ray Casting
definition: A ray casting technique that computes ray entry and exit points into a volume by rendering the volume's bounding box twice with different face culling and depth test modes, storing the results in separate depth/color attachments, then using these coordinates to cast rays through the volume in a third pass.
summary: Two-Pass Depth Ray Casting is a direct volume rendering technique that uses hardware rasterization to determine ray entry and exit points, separating depth determination from accumulation.
